newsitem.title: USA: Calif. unemployment rate drops to 6.5 pct - state.
newsitem.headline: Calif. unemployment rate drops to 6.5 pct - state.

text.p: California's unemployment rate dropped to 6.5 percent in April from a revised 6.6 percent in March and 7.4 percent in April 1996, according to a state report Friday.

The April report, released by the California Employment Development Department, was hailed by Gov. Pete Wilson. "California's economy is in the midst of a strong expansion," Wilson, a Republican, said in a statement.
The department said California businesses added 15,500 jobs since March. At this rate, the state will add over 400,000 jobs during the year, the department's report said.
Employment Development Department said seven industry groups added jobs in April, gaining 17,000 positions. Two industries -- mining and construction -- reported job declined totaling 1,500.
Most of the job growth was in the manufacturing sector, up 5,400 jobs. Services, finance, insurance, real estate and retail trade also posted gains, the department said.
The April employment report was yet another sign of California's economic strength.
Earlier this week, Wilson added $1.6 billion to his 1997-1998 budget proposal to aid cash-strapped local governments, boost education funding and help find jobs for welfare recipients.
Wilson said California's economy has grown so fast that he now expects state revenues in the current year and fiscal year 1997-1998 to top his previous budget forecast by $2.26 billion.
